overall_summary: A black bear moves from shoreline rocks into a loosely tied canoe. Grandma sees it from the cabin doorway, runs along a clear open ground path to the dock, and arrives too late as the canoe drifts downstream.
tone: Unplanned real-life outdoor security-camera footage: ordinary, observational, imperfect, and believable; never cinematic, staged, polished, promotional, or commercial.
capture_style: One fixed outdoor security-camera viewpoint with mild fisheye distortion, natural late-afternoon light, ordinary image quality, and no camera operator movement.
visual_style: Real lakeside cabin footage with a simple brown cabin on the left, visible side door, open ground path, shoreline rocks, short dock, one red canoe, and downstream lake bend.
visual_realism: The cabin door, ground path, rocks, dock, canoe, shoreline, and lake must form one physically continuous environment with believable scale and contact.
audio_policy: Natural location sound only: water, wood, rope strain, bear movement, footsteps, and distant birds.
camera_lock: Keep one completely fixed elevated security-camera viewpoint, with the cabin on the left, dock on the right, and lake moving toward the visible bend. No pan, tilt, zoom, cut, alternate angle, or geometry change.
continuity_invariants: Exactly one bear, one Grandma, one canoe, one dock, and one cabin remain throughout.
The bear's route is shoreline rocks to shoreline beside the canoe to inside the canoe to downstream water.
Grandma's route is the visible cabin doorway to the unobstructed ground path to the dock edge.
No railing, wall, hidden corner, stairs, fence, or obstacle blocks the path between the cabin door and dock.
